results.content: If there’s one parallel story that consistently rivals the AI doomsday discourse, it’s the seemingly simpler matter of scaling AI costs. From what we’ve been learning from customers, it is also the story that will impact the next phase of innovation the most. We believe that monetizing agents that perform complex, variable, long-horizon work must begin with a granular understanding of each agent run. Everything else—model selection, usage caps, managing margins—follows from that. Today, we’re introducing AUDR (Agent Usage Detail Record): an open specification for attributing who initiated an agent run and how much it cost, across every system that run touched. AUDR borrows both its name and premise from CDR (Call Detail Record), the decades-old telecom format that captures structured data [...] decades-old telecom format that captures structured data for every phone call. It’s CDRs that make interoperability between disparate regional and global carriers possible. Agent development needs that same shared standard across model providers, gateways, frameworks, and other parts of the stack. We’re working on adapters for NVIDIA NeMo Relay, Merge Gateway, Mastra, Verceleve, LiteLLM AI Gateway, OpenRouter, and others. We’re grateful for constructive, early reviews from teams at Merge, Mastra, TinyHumans, and others. And special thanks to Anand Chandrasekaran for his thoughtful review and inputs. Check out the spec (link below) and help us shape this new standard.
